americas_summary: The Americas face elevated exposure to energy and freight-price pressure, delayed or constrained maritime trade, critical-mineral shortages, and localized transport disruption. Evidence does not establish broad Americas-wide outages, shortages, payment failures, or access restrictions.
confidence_rationale: Fresh Tier A reporting directly supports maritime, energy, natural-hazard, and localized transport assessments; several trade, cyber, and regional-strike signals are older, forward-looking, or lower-tier. Evidence gate: 14 items, 12 sources, 8 Tier-A sources, 5/5 clusters.
summary: Severe, observed maritime-security disruption and energy-market tightness continue to drive cross-border preparedness risk; Americas-facing exposure remains high through fuel, shipping, commodity, and critical-mineral channels.
primary_driver: Escalating attacks and military activity affecting Hormuz and Black Sea shipping, compounded by tight global gas and critical-mineral supply.
primary_stabilizers: Quad ministers pledged stronger reliable supply chains and condemned coercive export restrictions, while planning business cooperation and resource pooling.
The Federal Reserve reported orderly Treasury and equity-market functioning, with liquidity recovering after earlier volatility and overnight funding remaining stable.
USGS lowered Shishaldin’s aviation color code to green, reporting declining unrest and no eruption expected from current activity.

signals.title: Hormuz strikes and vessel damage
signals.summary: U.S. strikes targeted Iranian positions in the Strait of Hormuz, while a vessel was reportedly damaged by an unknown projectile, increasing immediate maritime and energy-flow risks.

signals.title: Black Sea shipping attacks
signals.summary: Seven cargo ships were struck near NATO members Romania and Bulgaria last month; NATO is deploying maritime patrol aircraft, radars, and drones, while regional oil and grain exports have fallen.

signals.title: Gas security remains tight
signals.summary: The IEA says low European storage buffers and a projected 3% global LNG supply decline in 2026 could prolong tight gas markets into 2027 despite ongoing security coordination.

signals.title: Rare-earth access remains tight
signals.summary: Some Chinese rare-earth suppliers halted U.S. shipments, while yttrium, indium phosphide, and tungsten prices remained near records amid tight supply.

signals.title: Critical-mineral restrictions face deadline
signals.summary: Several U.S.–China tariff and export-control suspensions, including measures affecting critical minerals and semiconductors, are scheduled for review or expiration on November 10, 2026.

signals.title: Cyber risk to financial services
signals.summary: The Federal Reserve warns cyber events could disrupt financial services, degrade market liquidity, erode confidence, and trigger forced asset sales.

signals.title: Payment-system resilience
signals.summary: Federal Reserve research finds third-party payment-software outages can materially reduce affected banks’ Fedwire activity, though alternative channels provide partial resilience.

signals.title: Yucatán highway blockade
signals.summary: Protesters blocked Mexico’s Federal Highway 295 near Río Lagartos, prompting authorities to advise avoiding nearby communities and expect significant travel delays.

preparedness_actions: Complete sensible, previously planned preparedness purchases while normal supply channels are functioning.
Maintain several weeks of food, household consumables, water capacity, and essential medical supplies.
Keep vehicles reasonably fueled and verify generator, battery, solar, or other backup-power capability.
Maintain diversified payment options and a reasonable amount of emergency cash.
Confirm family communications, transportation, and meeting plans.
Avoid panic buying; focus on resilience gaps that would be difficult to correct after disruption begins.

methodology.note: All-hazards early-warning assessment. The score is a preparedness-urgency index, not the probability that a disaster, collapse, or war will occur.
methodology.formula: Preparedness Urgency = 40% Global Threat Pressure + 25% Observed Civilian Disruption + 10% Cross-System Coupling + 10% Momentum/Persistence + 15% Americas Exposure. Global threat, observed impact, and Americas exposure are weighted averages across all 12 domains.
methodology.rate_limits: Absent a verified hard trigger, normal daily movement is limited to ±3 points. A verified but non-severe hard trigger allows up to ±6. A verified national, multinational, or global hard trigger can bypass the rate limit.
methodology.stage_guardrails: HIGH ALERT begins at 80. IMMINENT DISRUPTION requires a score of at least 90, observed disruption of at least 75, and a verified severe hard trigger plus either 48-hour persistence or an active fast-onset trigger. ACTIVE DISRUPTION requires at least 97, observed disruption at least 85, three high-impact domains, and two verified severe triggers.
methodology.civil_unrest: Civil Unrest / Public Order is scored from observable violence, duration, geographic spread, emergency measures, infrastructure damage, and disruption to transport, commerce, public safety, or essential services. Peaceful protest and political ideology do not raise the score by themselves.
methodology.confidence: Evidence confidence is capped mechanically by source quality, recency, independence, cluster coverage, and actual web-search completion. It does not increase preparedness urgency.
methodology.pipeline: GPT-5.6 Luna collects current evidence in paced, low-context, one-search cluster requests to stay below TPM limits. GPT-5.6 Terra evaluates only validated evidence with no web access. JavaScript validates hard triggers and calculates the final score mechanically.
